summary: Iteration 4: refactor regression pass. Backend: 52/52 pytest pass (48 regression + 4 new in test_iter4_refactor.py). GET /api/games/{id} shape is unchanged for 3498 and 41494: screenshots are a list of URL strings, stores have name+url, developers, trailers and requirements are present, an unknown id gives 404. The split email guard rejects forms, credential asks, http, shorteners, IP hosts, userinfo and mismatched anchor text, and accepts a valid email. Cron reminder sends once to delivered@resend.dev (Email API 202). The first full run failed 1 cron test. That was a test-data problem, not an app bug: the new refresh_release_dates() reloads wishlist dates from RAWG, and the fake ids 990001-3 are real RAWG games (2024-10-02), so their 'today' date was overwritten. I changed the test to use ids that don't exist on RAWG (989999001-3). Frontend: AI Guide: 4 suggestions; a typed message streams into exactly one assistant bubble; send stays disabled while streaming even with text typed; history persists on reload; New chat resets to the suggestions; a suggestion click sends. minor.issue: Makes one sequential RAWG detail call per distinct wishlist game_id that has released >= 7 days ago or null. This includes every far-future game (e.g. 2099), so the cron gets slower and costs more RAWG quota as wishlists grow. Consider limiting it to dates within about ±14 days of today plus null, and use asyncio.gather with a semaphore

integration_issues.issue: Releases.jsx effect has no alive/abort guard (unlike useApi). Quickly switching platform or sort can let a late response overwrite or append stale results

rca of the issue: TestCron.test_run_sends_once failed with reminders_sent=0. Cause: the new refresh_release_dates() fetched RAWG /games/990001, which is a real game (Settlements Rising, released 2024-10-02), and overwrote the seeded 'today' date, so no item matched today.
